first_reader_source: PMC full text PMC2689518, the NIH author manuscript
title: Human cannabinoid pharmacokinetics

claims.statement: As summarised in a 2007 narrative review of controlled-administration studies, most of them small, in men who had used cannabis before, with single doses of low-THC cigarettes or of oral THC, and many from the author's own laboratory (Huestis, 2007; figures second-hand; no systematic search), smoking cannabis is associated with THC reaching the blood within minutes, eating it with slower, lower and later blood levels, and frequent use with THC staying in the body for days to weeks. Smoked: in 6 men who each smoked one cigarette of 1.75% or 3.55% THC (about 16 or 34 mg; study conditions), THC appeared in plasma with the first puff, peaked at a mean of 84.3 and 162.2 ng/ml at 9.0 minutes, fell to about 60% and 20% of the peak 15 and 30 minutes after smoking, and was 5 ng/ml or less within 2 hours, staying detectable (at 0.5 ng/ml) for 3 to 12 hours after the lower and 6 to 27 hours after the higher dose; the strongest effects came later, 30 to 45 minutes after smoking began, when blood levels were already falling. How much of the THC in a cigarette reached the blood varied with how people smoked, from 2% to 56% across studies (about 8% to 24% in others). Eaten: THC was absorbed more slowly, with lower, later and more irregular peaks; after 20 mg of THC in a chocolate cookie, plasma peaks of 4.4 to 11 ng/ml came 1 to 5 hours after eating, with about 6% of the dose reaching the blood, and a study using a radiolabel method, which the author says overestimated THC, found peaks about 4 to 6 hours after 15 to 20 mg in oil; the review puts oral bioavailability at 4% to 20%, because THC is partly broken down in the stomach and much of it is converted in the liver, among other products into 11-OH-THC, which is active and reaches levels similar to or higher than those of THC after eating, against about a tenth of THC after smoking. Compared with smoking, effects after eating began later and lasted longer. THC is almost entirely bound to lipoproteins in the blood (95% to 99%) and is stored in body fat; in people who use frequently, its final plasma half-life was about 4.1 days in a study with long sampling (24 to 36 hours in studies with shorter sampling), and THC-COOH, the breakdown product that urine tests measure, had a plasma half-life of up to 12.6 days in one person. Blood: in people who use frequently, low levels remain between uses (THC 0.86 ng/ml on average at least 12 hours after last use in one study), and a very sensitive method detected a labelled dose of THC for up to 13 days in people who used chronically. Urine: after one smoked cigarette, urine tested positive for THC-COOH at a cut-off of 15 ng/ml for an average of 33.7 hours (8 to 68.5) after the 1.75% and 88.6 hours (57 to 122.3) after the 3.55% cigarette, with positive and negative samples alternating near the cut-off; in two people with heavy use, urine stayed positive for up to 67 days (one person, at 20 ng/ml, after more than 10 years of heavy use) and 93 days. A positive urine test shows that a person was exposed, not when, how much, by which route or whether they were impaired. These studies predate today's stronger products, edibles, vaporizers and concentrates, mostly involved men and gave fixed doses, so they do not show what happens when people who feel little at first take more. Certainty: very low. Status: replicated.
claims.magnitude: Smoked (6 men): mean plasma THC peaks 84.3 ng/ml (range 50-129) and 162.2 ng/ml (76-267) at 9.0 minutes; about 60% and 20% of peak at 15 and 30 minutes; 5 ng/ml or less within 2 hours; detectable at 0.5 ng/ml for 3-12 and 6-27 hours; peak effects 30-45 minutes after smoking began; bioavailability 2%-56% (or about 8%-24%). Oral: 20 mg in a cookie, peaks 4.4-11 ng/ml at 1-5 hours, bioavailability about 6%; 15-20 mg in oil, peaks at about 4-6 hours (radiolabel); 10 mg dronabinol (17 volunteers), THC 3.8 ng/ml (1.1-12.7), 11-OH-THC 3.4 (1.2-5.6), THC-COOH 26 (14-46) at 1-2 hours; summary bioavailability 4%-20%; 11-OH-THC about 10% of THC after smoking, similar or higher after eating. Elimination: terminal plasma THC half-life about 4.1 days with frequent use (24-36 hours with shorter sampling); THC-COOH plasma half-life up to 12.6 days in one person; frequent use, plasma THC 0.86 ng/ml at least 12 hours after last use; deuterated THC detectable up to 13 days (limit 0.02 ng/ml). Urine (6 men, 15 ng/ml cut-off): last positive 33.7 hours (8-68.5) and 88.6 hours (57-122.3) after one cigarette; heavy use, up to 67 days (20 ng/ml) and 93 days in two individuals.
